> ECHO//SENTRY is a compact real-time object detection and spatial awareness system built around an Arduino microcontroller, ultrasonic distance sensing, and servo-based scanning. The system continuously sweeps an ultrasonic sensor across a defined angular range, measures the distance to nearby objects, and transmits the collected spatial data to a computer over serial communication. A custom live visualization converts the sensor readings into a radar-style interface, displaying: Current scanning angle Detected object distance Approximate object position Detection zones Real-time sweep animation Serial sensor telemetry Configurable detection range The project demonstrates the integration of embedded systems, sensor interfacing, servo control, serial communication, signal acquisition, data visualization, and basic spatial detection into a single working prototype. Important technical note: this is an ultrasonic radar-style system, not electromagnetic radar.
